visual.detailed_description: White background. A light-blue rounded box at the left reads "Type 2 Diabetes". Seven dotted arrows lead from it to colored boxes with small organ icons. Green box (liver icon): "Hepatic glucose production" with an up arrow, listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist", "Metformin" and "TZD". Orange box (kidney icon): "Glucose resorption" with an up arrow, listing "SGLT2 inhbitors" (printed spelling). Gold box (pancreas icon): "α-cell: ↑ glucagon secretion", listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist", "DPP4i" and "Pramlintide"; a neighbouring gold box to its right (pancreas icon, no separate arrow from the central box seen): "β-cell: ↓ insulin secretion", listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist", "DPP4i" and "TZD". Pale yellow box (human figure icon): "Peripheral glucose uptake" with a down arrow, listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist" and "TZD". Blue box (fat cells icon): "Increased lipolysis", listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist" and "TZD". Purple box (brain icon): "Neurotransmitter dysfunction", listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist", "Pramlintide" and "Insulin". Magenta box (intestine icon): "Incretin effect" with a down arrow listing "GLP-1 receptor agonist", then "Carbohydrate absorption" listing "AGI" and "Gastric emptying" listing "Pramlintide". No patient data, scale, panel letters, faces or identifying text are visible.

visual.general_description: Colored flow diagram of renal SGLT2 inhibition leading to glycosuria and natriuresis effects that converge on cardiac and renal protection, with a nephron and tubule-cell schematic at the top.
visual.detailed_description: White background. Top left: a line drawing of a nephron with a small boxed region linked by dashed lines to an enlarged cell schematic titled "Proximal Convoluted Tubule" with "Lumen" at left and "Blood" at right. In the cell, a large blue circle labelled "SGLT-2" carries arrows for "Glucose" and "Na+" into the cell from the lumen, with a red inhibition bar at the transporter; on the blood side are green ovals "ATPase" and "GLUT2" and a "K+" arrow. Beneath, red underlined text "SGLT-2 inhibitors" has two dotted arrows labelled "RENAL" to an orange-outlined box "Glycosuria" and a green-outlined box "Natriuresis". Glycosuria leads to three gold ovals: "Reduced adipose tissue", "Better glycemic profile" and "Increased uric acid in urine". Natriuresis leads to three blue ovals: "Reduced blood pressure", "Reduced tubuloglomerular feedback" and "Reduced plasma volume". Lower boxes: green "HEART" ("Improved function", "Reduced epicardial fat"), green "GLUCOSE" ("↓ Oxidative stress", "↓ Glucotoxicity", "↓ Atherosclerosis"), green "METABOLISM" ("Reduced uric acid in plasma"), purple "VASCULAR PROFILE" ("↓ Arterial stiffness", "Afferent arteriole constriction"), purple "HEART" ("↓ Myocardial strecth" (printed spelling), "↓ Cardiac arrhythmias"). Outcome boxes: blue "↓ Cardiac fibrosis" and "↓ Cardiac inflammation", red "↓ Intraglomerular hypertension" and "↓ Hyperfiltration", yellow "- Activation of ACE2 - Ang1/7" and "- No sympathetic nervous system activation". Dotted arrows from all branches converge on underlined text "Cardiac and Renal Protection" at the bottom centre. No patient data, panel letters, faces or identifying text are visible.
